audit.reasoning: Coding (fixed penultimate, '10 010 0010 00010', dominant not strict) is supported by every source opened, but the record's only citation is a Wikipedia family-article sentence about the Sinama (Inner Sulu) languages, third-hand from Pallesen 1985:124, with empty cite/loc/grade fields; Mapun is classified as Borneo Coast Bajaw, so that sentence does not strictly cover it. Mapun-specific confirmation now held: SIL's own Mapun Dictionary web edition Grammar page ('stress is on the penultimate syllable') and a page explicitly summarising Collins et al. 2001 ('Mapun words have predictable stress on the penultimate syllable'); Kaufman's handbook chapter confirms right-aligned trochaic stress with suffixes/enclitics inside the window for SB generally. No grammar, phonology paper or acoustic study of Mapun exists (Glottolog 0 descriptive refs; Ingilan & Jubilado say no reference grammar; SIL arc
audit.second_reader_evidence: Quote finding verified: held=[]; the record's only source is Wikipedia 'Mapun language' -> redirect 'Sama–Bajaw languages', Stress section, verbatim 'all of the Sinama languages primary stress occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word.[3]:124 Stress will remain on the penultimate syllable even with the addition of suffixes including enclitic pronouns' (saved) — a Sinama-scope, third-hand statement; cite/loc/grade empty. The other first reader's readings of its fetched sources files also check out verbatim: SIL Webonary Mapun Dictionary Grammar page 'Typology: VSO; stress is on the penultimate syllable' (Phonology page empty); iloko.tripod

sources.quote: all of the Sinama languages primary stress occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word. ... Stress will remain on the penultimate syllable even with the addition of suffixes including enclitic pronouns.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Sama–Bajaw languages' (redirect target of 'Mapun language'), Stress section, fetched sources 2026-09-16.
sources.quote: 'all of the Sinama languages primary stress occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word.[3]:124 Stress will remain on the penultimate syllable even with the addition of suffixes including enclitic pronouns. In Northern Sinama (Balanguingi) the stress will shift to the ultima when the penult is the mid central vowel /ə/.' Matches the record's quoted text; scope is Sinama, not Mapun.

sources.quote: 'Vowel length is designated with a macron over the vowel (not standardized). ... Mapun words have predictable stress on the penultimate syllable. Unlike Tausug, with three contrastive vowels, Mapun have five contrastive vowels.'

sources.citation: Kaufman, Daniel. to appear. The Sama-Bajaw languages. In A. Schapper & S. Adelaar (eds.), Oxford Handbook of Western Austronesian Languages. OUP. (author preprint v4, 8 pp.)
sources.quote: 'No SB language shows the phonemic vowel length distinction in penultimate syllables characteristic of Philippine languages. Rather, most SB languages have been described as having a right-aligned trochaic, stress pattern. Some varieties, such as Pangutaran Sama, have been further described as having iterative secondary stress preceding the primary stress on the penultimate syllable (Pallesen 1979:192). The stress window includes suffixes and genitive pronominal enclitics.' Family-level; Mapun not singled out.
sources.locator: sec. 2, p.3, with ex. (2) from Pallesen 1985:94
